newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Market perks up.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Market perks up.

text.p: Asian debt markets perked up on Tuesday after starting the week slowly.
South Korea's Daedong Bank launched a US$50 million callable, step-up subordinated floating rate note issue via lead manager Merrill Lynch Far East.

The bond has a final maturity of 10 years but can be called on the fifth anniversary. It pays a semi-annual coupon of 85 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate for the first five years and 190 basis points over LIBOR for years six through 10.
At the re-offer price the notes yield 86.5 basis point to the call.
This structure has become popular among South Korean banks eager to boost tier two capital.
Hong Kong's First Pacific Bank launched a US$35 million dual-currency floating rate certificate of deposit issue. Banks can participate in either Hong Kong or U.S. dollars or in both.
Both the Hong Kong dollar and U.S. dollar tranches have final maturities of five years but can be put or called in years three and four.
The Hong Kong dollar tranche pays a coupon of 79 basis points over the three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate and an all-in return of 106 basis points to top-tier managers.
The U.S. dollar tranche pays a coupon of 60 basis points over three-month LIBOR and an all-in return of 87 basis points.
CS First Boston Hong Kong and Credit Lyonnais Hong Kong are arrangers.

First Pacific Bank is wholly held by FPB Holdings, which in turn is 41.25 percent held and controlled by First Pacific Co. A minority state in the company is held by Chinese entities that report directly to China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation (MOFTEC).
The issue stipulates that First Pacific Co must maintain effective majority shareholding of the issuer and in any event not less than 35 percent.

In March, First Pacific Bank launched a dual-currency FRCD with a three-year maturity and two-year put that paid an all-in of 100 basis points for the Hong Kong dollar tranche and an all-in of 80 basis points for the U.S. dollar tranche. That issue did not include a call option.
Looking ahead, China Travel Services Hong Kong has mandated LTCB Asia and Sanwa International Finance to arrange a US$150 million FRN.
Indonesian timber company PT Surya Dumai Industri launched a US$75 million floating rate note issue through BT Asia. The five-year deal has puts in year three.
It pays a coupon of 250 basis points over LIBOR and an all-in return of 300 basis points to the top tier.
Another Indonesian firm, Medco Energi, plans to launch a US$50 million FRN. Dongsuh Securities is the arranger.
Elsewhere, rumours were circulating that South Korea's KEXIM is mulling a Yankee bond. Lehman Brothers is tipped to be the lead, but it declined to comment on the deal.
